title: HTTP routes from a macro
blurb: The app declares its routes once, as a token stream: method, name, path pattern, query struct. The macro reads the rows with a token cursor and emits a sum type with one variant per route, an allocation-free trie matcher that percent-decodes, and a printer back to a URL. Dispatch is a match on that type, and a mistake in a row is reported at the offending token in your file.

blocks.label: the routes
blocks.code:
$http/routing/define(route, \{
  get    home         "/"
  get    events       "/events"
  get    counter      "/counter/events"
  get    big-file     "/static/big-file.json"
  get    starry       "/app/starry-night"
  get    visits       "/visits" ?{ who: ?string }
  post   login        "/login"
  get    game-events  "/game/{id: u64}/events"
  post   game-poke    "/game/{id: u64}/poke"
  delete delete-game  "/game/{id: u64}"
})

blocks.label: the macro
what comes out
blocks.code:
if route/parse-request(req.header) is {
    :err e -> error-response(e),
    :ok r -> if r is {
      :home -> home-page(),
      :events -> global-events(deps),
      :counter -> counter-events(),
      :game-events .{ id } -> game-events(deps, id),
      :game-poke .{ id } -> game-poke(deps, id),
      :big-file -> big-file(),
      :starry -> response/html("todo"),
      :visits p -> visits(deps, req, p.who),
      :login -> login(req),
      :delete-game p -> response/html("todo ${p.id}"),
    }
  }

title: JSON from reflection
blurb: json/to-string is library code with no compiler support. It reads the type's schema at compile time and generates a writer for exactly these fields, the nested sum and the optional included.

blocks.label: the type
blocks.code:
type contact = either { email(string), phone(string), unreachable }
type person = { name: string, age: u32, nickname: ?string, contact: contact }

blocks.label: to JSON
blocks.code: println(json/to-string(ada))

blocks.label: output
blocks.code: {"name":"Ada Lovelace","age":36,"nickname":null,"contact":{"email":"ada@example.com"}}

title: Abilities, not inheritance
blurb: Abilities are k1's typeclasses: ad-hoc polymorphism without a hierarchy. Implement one for a type you did not write, bound a generic on it, or implement it once for every type that has another. Operators are abilities too, so operator overloading is implementing add for your type. Dispatch is static unless you ask for dyn.

title: Types from a .proto file
blurb: A .proto file is read at compile time, parsed by ordinary k1 running in the compile-time VM, and turned into a struct and an enum with types/make-struct and types/make-either. The subset is small, one message of scalar and enum fields and one enum, and the result is a real k1 type: exhaustive matching, layout, everything.

blocks.label: user.proto
derive
blocks.code:
type(alias) status = #type proto/enum("user.proto", "Status")
type(alias) user = #type proto/message("user.proto", "User")

blocks.label: use
output
blocks.code:
7 ada 99.5 suspended=1 on hold
size 36 status 4

title: A keyword recognizer, generated
blurb: gperf as a macro. Hand it the words and it searches for a perfect hash over character positions, then emits a sum type and a recognizer that is a few loads, a mask and a compare.

blocks.label: the words
blocks.code: $keywords/define(tiny, ["if", "in", "is", "fn", "for"])

blocks.label: lookup
blocks.code: println("${tiny/lookup("for")} ${tiny/lookup("fun")}")

blocks.label: output
blocks.code: :some kw-for :none

title: A regex engine that runs at compile time
blurb: Parser, NFA, DFA and minimization are plain k1 that happens to run in the compiler. A define becomes a matcher whose states are match arms, plus a finder that returns match positions.

blocks.label: define
blocks.code: $regex/define(number, "[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?")

blocks.label: match and find
output

number("3.14") = true
number("3.") = false
number(".5") = false
number("1e5") = false

title: Painless SIMD
blurb: A macro generates a lane-wide scanner for a set of delimiters, the scan loop uses it like any function, and the same code runs under #static in the compile-time VM.

blocks.label: generate the scanner
blocks.code: $std/simd/first-of(delims, [',', ':', '"'])

blocks.label: use it
at compile time too
blocks.code:
let static-hits: 4u64 = #static scan-all-simd("{\"key\": [1, 2]}")
  println("compile-time scan found ${static-hits.from-static()} delimiters")

title: C at compile time
